text:
morgan: FYI — I opened an RFC to deprecate the legacy penalty connector (penalty-store-v1) and replace it with a simplified penalty-aggregator + granularity sweep. TL;DR: reduce coupling between policy compiler and runtime heuristics, and let runtime opt into coarser/finer buckets dynamically.
anya: can you summarize the main compatibility risks?
morgan: main risks: 1) callers expecting bucketed penalty payload shape (nested map) will break; 2) probes that relied on fine-grained tids for decay schedules; 3) telemetry dashboards need remapping. The plan uses a compatibility shim in the router for 6 weeks.
lee: how different is the new shape? example pls.
morgan: new payload is intentionally flatter: `{"penalty_score": 0.32, "scope": "region:us-east,tenant:xyz", "ttl_secs": 120}` vs old `{"buckets": [{"id":"latency","score":0.2},{"id":"cost","score":0.12}], "decay":{"per_bucket":true}}`
lee: ok that is much simpler to reason about at runtime. what about policy authors who compose penalties from multiple plugins?
devon: proposal: keep plugin authoring surface the same in the DSL but change compiler lowering to emit per-plugin contributions + an aggregator stage. That way authors don't rewrite rules, compiler teams change, runtime receives flat contributions and aggregator reduces to a single `penalty_score` per route.
anya: aggregator semantics need to be explicit — is it sum? max? weighted?
morgan: agree. RFC proposes a pluggable aggregation strategy with default = weighted-sum where weights are normalized by tenant SLA. Plugins can declare their intended aggregation kind but runtime can override via policy flags.
samir: we should be careful about reproducibility. current multi-bucket approach lets us explain per-bucket contributions. Flat score loses that visibility.
devon: good point — aggregator will keep an internal debug vector that we emit to the debug/trace span and to a low QPS telemetry channel (sampled) so we can still attribute regressions. Not in the fast path.
anya: rollout strategy?
morgan: steps: 1) compile-time: add deprecation warnings when DSL lowers to legacy payload shape (canary rule set for 2 weeks). 2) router shim: accept both shapes and normalize to aggregator input. 3) infra: enable new aggregator module behind `feature.penalty_aggregator` flag. 4) telemetry: dual-emission for 4 weeks — old metrics + new aggregated metrics. 5) cutover: flip flag for 10% traffic, monitor, ramp. 6) deprecation: after 6 weeks post-cutover, remove shim.
samir: metrics checklist?
morgan: latency p99, extra CPU on router, penalty delta distribution, rollback rate, explainability regressions (eval set scores), and canary-specific quality evals.
lee: what about performance? the legacy connector had some vectorized ops optimized in C++ that we might lose if we do aggregation in Rust shim.
devon: aggregator implementation plan: a fast path in C++/CUDA for weighted-sum of large plugin vectors, with a fallback pure-Rust implementation. We'll benchmark both. The runtime already links the C++ lib for batching kernels so adding this should be low friction.
anya: any schema versioning? how will we mark payloads?
morgan: yes, every penalty payload will carry `schema_version` and `source_hint`. Router normalizer honors up-to-date versions. Old v1 entries get `schema_version: "v1"` and will be accepted by shim. New payloads set `v2`.
samir: testing — need sandboxed end-to-end test that asserts identical route decisions for a curated set of inputs under both v1 and v2 (within epsilon). Also need property tests for aggregator math.
devon: adding integration tests to routing-sim harness and a fuzz target that mutates plugin outputs.
anya: who owns this?
morgan: owning teams: compiler: @lee for lowering changes; runtime/router: @devon for aggregator & shim; infra: @samir for telemetry dual-write and dashboards. I'll keep coordination and timeline.
lee: estimate timeline?
morgan: prototype aggregator + shim in 2 weeks, internal canary in week 3, 10% traffic week 4, ramp over week 5-6. Final removal in week 12 to allow support escalations.
samir: notify customers with tenant-specific penalties (finance, ads) — we should prepare a migration guide and offer a support window.
anya: docs and migration: add DSL deprecation notes, example lowerings, and a troubleshooting runbook when aggregated penalty changes route selection.
devon: ops playbook: `feature.penalty_aggregator` toggle, revert path to route-ingress code, and script to rehydrate legacy buckets for historical debug.
\morgan: infra-bot — create alert template for penalty delta > 0.05 change in route score for top 50 routes in 10m window.
infra-bot: created alert `penalty-aggregator-delta` with severity=high, channels=#eng-oncall,#architecture`
samir: any open questions? I still worry about fairness across tenants if aggregator weights leak tenant-level SLA signals.
lee: runtime should normalize weights per-tenant and then apply global fairness clamp — added to RFC.
anya: sounds reasonable. let's sync tomorrow 11am to finalize the rollout doc and owners.
morgan: thanks — I'll update the RFC with these notes and add the canary test vectors.
lee: thanks all.
